title: The cycle of sacrifice and the example of the great

verses.sa: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
verses.tr: By nurturing the radiant beings through this duty, let them nurture you. Nurturing one another, you will attain the highest good.
verses.speaker: Unknown

intro.text: Krishna continues the cycle of giving, showing how duty creates a bond of mutual care. Listen for the two sides of this exchange.

body.text: By nurturing the radiant beings through this duty, let them nurture you. Nurturing one another, you will attain the highest good. Nourish the devas and they will nourish you; mutual care leads to the highest good. Krishna then warns that anyone who takes these gifts without giving back is nothing but a thief.

verses.sa: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
verses.tr: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief.
verses.angle: The thief who takes without giving back
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers a quiet question many people ask: why is sacrifice necessary, and what happens when we stop giving back? Listen to how he answers.

body.text: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief. The verse turns on a single Sanskrit word, apradaya, which means without giving back. It names the exact moment when a person stops participating in the exchange of life and becomes a thief. The next verse draws a sharp line between those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice and those who cook only for themselves.

verses.sa: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
verses.tr: Those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice are freed from all faults. Those who cook only for themselves eat only wrongdoing.
verses.angle: pachanti means cooking and eating sin
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna contrasts two ways of eating. One leads to freedom, the other to sin. Listen to how the word for cooking is turned into a word for eating wrongdoing.

body.text: Those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice are freed from all faults. Those who cook only for themselves eat only wrongdoing. The verb pachanti means to cook. Krishna says those who cook only for their own sake eat only agha, wrongdoing. The act of preparing food becomes the act of consuming sin. The cycle of action and return is explained next, beginning with food itself.

verses.sa: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
verses.tr: All beings arise from food. Food comes from rain. Rain comes from sacrifice. Sacrifice arises from action.
verses.angle: Annat, the first link in the chain
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one word that begins a long chain of life. Listen for where this chain starts.

body.text: All beings arise from food. Food comes from rain. Rain comes from sacrifice. Sacrifice arises from action. The chain begins with a single word, annat, from food. Food is the first link, and from it all beings come into being, so the whole world rests on what we eat and how it is produced. Krishna then asks Arjuna to see how action itself is born from the Vedas and the imperishable.

verses.sa: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
verses.tr: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is always established in sacrifice.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown how sacrifice sustains all life. Now He traces action back to its source. Listen for how the chain of existence is rooted in the divine.

body.text: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is always established in sacrifice. Notice the word viddhi, know. Krishna commands Arjuna to know that action is born from the Vedas, and the Vedas from the imperishable, making sacrifice the root of all existence. If anyone ignores this cycle of sacrifice and action, they live only for the senses and their life becomes empty.

verses.sa: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
verses.tr: O Partha, the one who does not follow this cycle set in motion here lives in vain, delighting only in the senses and living a life of wrongdoing.
verses.angle: Agha, a life tainted by wrongdoing
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains how life itself depends on a shared cycle of action. Listen to the warning he gives about refusing that order.

body.text: O Partha, the one who does not follow this cycle set in motion here lives in vain, delighting only in the senses and living a life of wrongdoing. The word indriyarama, delighting in the senses, names the one who refuses the cycle. He seeks pleasure alone and therefore lives a life that is agha, tainted by wrongdoing. Krishna now speaks of the one who has already found the true self, and so has no duty left to perform.

verses.sa: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
verses.tr: The person who delights in the true self, is satisfied in the true self, and is content in the true self has no duty left.
verses.angle: Karyam: duty that is no longer needed
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If work is for the world, what happens when the world is no longer needed? Listen for the one who has found fullness within.

body.text: The person who delights in the true self, is satisfied in the true self, and is content in the true self has no duty left. Krishna points to the one who has found fullness within. For this person, no duty remains to be done. Krishna then asks what the perfected person, who has no purpose in doing, should do next.

verses.sa: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन । न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
verses.tr: For the perfected person, no purpose remains in doing, and no purpose remains in not doing. No being in the world is a source of personal gain.
verses.angle: No purpose in acting or not acting
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Picture a person who needs nothing. Krishna says that for such a one, acting and resting are the same. Listen for who this person is.

body.text: For the perfected person, no purpose remains in doing, and no purpose remains in not doing. No being in the world is a source of personal gain. For the one who is complete, Krishna says, doing and not doing both gain nothing. Krishna then commands Arjuna to always perform his duty without attachment, because acting this way leads to the supreme.

verses.sa: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment; by acting without attachment, a person reaches the supreme.
verses.angle: asaktah: the word that frees every action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the person who needs nothing. Now he turns that into practice, telling Arjuna to act steadily. Listen for the single condition he places on every action.

body.text: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment; by acting without attachment, a person reaches the supreme. Listen to the word asaktah, without attachment. Krishna places this condition on every duty, and by doing so he makes freedom from clinging the very path to the supreme. Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself, and you should act too.

verses.sa: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
verses.tr: Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself. You should act too, while keeping the welfare of the world in view.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns from private hesitation to public duty. Listen to how he names the great figures who proved action leads to perfection.

body.text: Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself. You should act too, while keeping the welfare of the world in view. The verse names Janaka and others, janakaadayah, meaning Janaka and the rest. These are the great kings and sages who proved that perfection comes through action. Krishna reminds Arjuna that he must act for the welfare of the world, lokasangraha, just as great figures have done.

verses.sa: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world copies.
verses.angle: Shreshtha sets the standard for everyone
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by explaining why Arjuna must act, reminding him that his conduct is watched by the world.

body.text: Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world copies. The word shreshtha, the best, is the key here. It is not about being the strongest, but about being the most respected, and your example becomes the standard that everyone else copies. Krishna then asks Partha how the world would be led if he, the best, were to stop working.

verses.sa: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
verses.tr: O Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I have not yet gained that must be gained. Yet I remain engaged in action.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Why does Krishna keep fighting if he needs nothing? This verse answers that question by naming his very own reason for acting.

body.text: O Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I have not yet gained that must be gained. Yet I remain engaged in action. He says he has no duty left in the three worlds and no desire left to fulfill, yet he still engages in action. This shows that action does not need a personal reward to be right. He then warns that if he stops acting, the whole world will copy that laziness.

verses.sa: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
verses.tr: For if I ever stopped acting with care, people would follow my path in every way, Arjuna.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that he works with care because everyone watches him. Listen for the warning hidden inside that reason.

body.text: For if I ever stopped acting with care, people would follow my path in every way, Arjuna. Here he says that if he ever stopped working, people would copy that inaction, and he would be the cause of disorder. He then explains that if he stopped, the whole world would fall into ruin.

verses.sa: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् । सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
verses.tr: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would create disorder and destroy these people.
verses.angle: sankarasy: the word that names social collapse
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna says his own inaction would ruin the worlds. Listen for the word that names this ruin.

body.text: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would create disorder and destroy these people. This verse uses the word sankarasy, of mixed confusion. Krishna says his own inaction would create this same social disorder that Arjuna feared, proving that action is the only way to prevent collapse. Krishna now says the wise should act like the ignorant, but without attachment, to set an example for the world.
